notes: All 13 pass and the work looks genuine: the body goes beyond the asserted numbers (it also names the FixedWindowLimiter export break, the latency-for-delivery trade, and that neither change was measured alone), and the final message flags the export rename as a review risk. Weak spots in the eval rather than the run: (1) the test-pass assertion is graded from the executor's own prose summary of its shell session, not a raw tool log, so a run that misreported make test would pass undetected; (2) the 20-word lede bound was hit exactly, so the assertion gives no signal on whether the skill trims leads or just lands on the line; (3) no assertion checks that the PR body does not misattribute the 91.2%->99.1% gain to the backoff alone, which this run correctly handled ('Neither change was measured on its own') but a weaker run could repeat from the stale body while still passing every listed check; (4) nothing checks that the agent surfaced the breaking export rename, which is the one review-relevant fact a stale-body rewrite could easily drop.
